A law of 1869 authorized the government to create teacher-training schools, and Sarmiento and his minister Nicolás Avellaneda established the one in Paraná by decree of June 13, 1870, the first national normal school, which began classes in 1871 with the American George Stearns as its first director. It trained the teachers who spread common education throughout the country and was a center for the dissemination of positivism.

hechos/inauguracion-del-observatorio-de-.texto: Inauguration of the National Observatory of Córdoba

Sarmiento inaugurated the National Observatory in Córdoba on October 24, 1871, directed by the American astronomer Benjamin Apthorp Gould. Its astronomers cataloged the stars of the southern sky in the Argentine Uranometry (1879) and in later catalogs, and in 1872 the Oficina Meteorológica Argentina was created beside it.

hechos/fiebre-amarilla-1871/titulo.texto: Yellow Fever Epidemic in Buenos Aires

hechos/fiebre-amarilla-1871/resumen.texto: Between January and June 1871 yellow fever killed about 14,000 people in Buenos Aires, close to 8 percent of the population, and a large part of the inhabitants fled the city. A Popular Commission presided over by José Roque Pérez organized care for the sick, and among the dead were physicians such as Francisco Javier Muñiz; the Chacarita cemetery was opened to bury the victims. The epidemic accelerated the works for running water and sewers and, according to the most widespread interpretation, the move of wealthy families from the south of the city to the north.

hechos/revolucion-de-1874/resumen.texto: After the 1874 elections, which Avellaneda and the Partido Autonomista Nacional won, Mitre and his Partido Nacionalista denounced fraud and rose up on September 24, 1874. Mitre was defeated at La Verde, in the province of Buenos Aires (November 26), and surrendered; José Miguel Arredondo, who had risen in the interior, was defeated by Julio A. Roca at Santa Rosa, in Mendoza (December 7). The leaders were tried and later amnestied.

hechos/revolucion-de-1880/resumen.texto: Roca’s presidential candidacy set the national government against the governor of Buenos Aires, Carlos Tejedor, who assembled provincial militias; Avellaneda left the city and settled in Belgrano. Between June 20 and 21, 1880, the fighting at Barracas, Puente Alsina, and Los Corrales left between 2,000 and 3,000 dead, according to different estimates, and thousands wounded. Tejedor resigned, and in September Congress enacted Ley 1029, which federalized the city of Buenos Aires.

hechos/fundacion-de-la-plata/resumen.texto: After the federalization of the city of Buenos Aires, the province needed a new capital, and Governor Dardo Rocha laid the cornerstone of La Plata on November 19, 1882, a city planned in advance, with a grid layout, diagonal avenues, and monumental public buildings. Within a few years the provincial government, the Museo de La Plata, and later the university were installed there.

hechos/congreso-pedagogico-1882/resumen.texto: Roca’s government convened in Buenos Aires, in April and May 1882, a congress of educators from the country and abroad, presided over by Onésimo Leguizamón. Its conclusions in favor of free, compulsory, and graded primary education, and its debates on religious instruction, paved the way for Ley 1420 of 1884.

hechos/ruptura-con-el-vaticano-1884/titu.texto: Break in Relations with the Vatican

hechos/ruptura-con-el-vaticano-1884/resu.texto: In 1884 the vicar capitular of Córdoba, Jerónimo Clara, forbade Catholic families from sending their daughters to the normal school of that city, which was run by American Protestant women teachers, and the government removed him. The apostolic delegate Luigi Matera backed him and attacked the common education law, and on October 14, 1884 Roca expelled him from the country; relations with the Holy See remained broken until 1900.

hechos/leyes-laicas/resumen.texto: Between 1884 and 1888 the Partido Autonomista Nacional enacted Ley 1420 of common education, the Ley de Registro Civil of the Capital (1884), which took from the parishes the registration of births and deaths, and the Ley de Matrimonio Civil (1888). Catholics, led by José Manuel Estrada and Pedro Goyena, fought them in Congress, in the press, and in the Asamblea de los Católicos Argentinos (1884), and founded the Unión Católica.

hechos/fundacion-de-la-union-civica/resu.texto: On September 1, 1889 a rally of young people at the Jardín Florida in Buenos Aires founded the Unión Cívica de la Juventud against the government of Juárez Celman, and on April 13, 1890 a large event at the Frontón Buenos Aires created the Unión Cívica, which brought together Mitrists, Catholics, dissident Autonomists, and young people under the presidency of Leandro Alem. Three months later it organized the revolution of the Parque.

hechos/crisis-de-1890/resumen.texto: During the 1880s Argentina borrowed abroad for public works, railways, and banks, while the Ley de Bancos Garantidos multiplied paper money and the stock exchange was swept by a wave of speculation. In 1890 gold soared and the government could not pay the debt service; in November the Baring Brothers house in London, heavily exposed to Argentine securities, had to be rescued by the Bank of England, and in 1891 the Banco Nacional and the Banco de la Provincia de Buenos Aires failed. The crisis brought about the fall of Juárez Celman, the moratorium of 1891, and the creation of the Caja de Conversión and the Banco de la Nación.

hechos/creacion-del-banco-de-la-nacion/t.texto: Creation of the Banco de la Nación Argentina

hechos/creacion-del-banco-de-la-nacion/r.texto: After the failure of the Banco Nacional and the Banco de la Provincia de Buenos Aires in the crisis of 1890, Pellegrini’s government created the Banco de la Nación Argentina by law of October 1891, which opened its doors on December 1 of that year. It became the main state bank and a source of credit for commerce and the countryside.

hechos/revolucion-de-1893/resumen.texto: In July 1893 the Radicals led by Hipólito Yrigoyen rose up in the province of Buenos Aires with thousands of armed civilians and took La Plata, and in San Luis and Santa Fe they also overthrew the governments. In September a second revolution in Santa Fe, with Alem and with the participation of farm settlers, took Rosario, and was defeated by the national troops under Roca. The government of Luis Sáenz Peña intervened in the provinces, declared a state of siege, and jailed Alem.

hechos/revolucion-de-1905/resumen.texto: On February 4, 1905 the Unión Cívica Radical, led by Hipólito Yrigoyen, rose up with the support of army officers in Buenos Aires, Bahía Blanca, Córdoba, Mendoza, and Santa Fe to end electoral fraud. In Córdoba the rebels took as hostages, among others, Vice President Figueroa Alcorta. Quintana’s government suppressed the movement within a few days and declared a state of siege, but in 1906 Congress amnestied the revolutionaries.

hechos/clausura-del-congreso-1908/titulo.texto: Closing of Congress by Figueroa Alcorta

hechos/clausura-del-congreso-1908/lugar.texto: Palacio del Congreso de la Nación

hechos/clausura-del-congreso-1908/resume.texto: In January 1908, with Congress dominated by Roca’s supporters and no budget approved for that year, President Figueroa Alcorta declared the extraordinary sessions ended, and the police occupied the Congress building. By decree he extended the previous year’s budget, and in the March elections his supporters won the majority.

hechos/conventillos-de-buenos-aires/resu.texto: With mass immigration, a large part of Buenos Aires’s workers lived in conventillos, old townhouses or new buildings with rooms rented to entire families, arranged around courtyards with shared bathrooms and washbasins. The municipal censuses of 1887 and 1904 recorded thousands of conventillos, which housed a significant part of the city’s population. Hygienists such as Guillermo Rawson identified them as breeding grounds for epidemics, and high rents led to the tenants’ strike of 1907.

hechos/primer-primero-de-mayo-1890/titul.texto: First May Day rally in Argentina

hechos/primer-primero-de-mayo-1890/resum.texto: On May 1, 1890, following the call of the Second International, the German socialist club Vorwärts and other workers’ associations, mostly made up of immigrants, held a rally at the Prado Español in Buenos Aires, and there were others in Rosario, Bahía Blanca and Chivilcoy. The petition approved asked Congress for labor protection laws, such as the eight-hour day and a ban on work by children under 14, and the organizing committee gave rise to the country’s first workers’ federation.

hechos/huelga-general-de-1902/resumen.texto: In November 1902 a strike by stevedores and cart drivers at the port of Buenos Aires spread into a general strike called by the Federación Obrera Argentina, the country’s first. On November 22 Congress passed the Ley de Residencia in a single session, which allowed the expulsion of foreigners considered dangerous, and the Roca government declared a state of siege.

hechos/huelga-de-inquilinos-1907/resumen.texto: In August 1907, faced with rising rents, tenants in the conventillos of Buenos Aires stopped paying, and the movement spread for about three months to more than a hundred tenement houses and to other cities, such as Rosario and Bahía Blanca. It was driven by anarchists and socialists, and women played a central role, resisting evictions with brooms. Ramón Falcón’s police carried out forced evictions, and during one of them the young Miguel Pepe was killed.

hechos/primer-congreso-femenino-1910/res.texto: Between May 18 and 23, 1910, within the framework of the Centenary, the Asociación Universitarias Argentinas hosted in Buenos Aires a congress of women from several countries, presided over by Cecilia Grierson. It debated women’s education, women’s work, the reform of the Civil Code, which placed the married woman under her husband’s authority, and women’s suffrage.

hechos/descubrimiento-del-petroleo-en-co.texto: On December 13, 1907 a national government drilling project looking for water at Comodoro Rivadavia struck oil. The next day Figueroa Alcorta set aside a wide area around the well for the State, the beginning of state-run exploitation that in 1922 was organized as Yacimientos Petrolíferos Fiscales (YPF).

hechos/laudo-hayes/titulo.texto: Boundary treaty with Paraguay and the Hayes award

hechos/laudo-hayes/resumen.texto: Under the Machaín-Irigoyen treaty of 1876, Argentina and Paraguay fixed their boundaries: Argentina kept Misiones and the Chaco between the Bermejo and the Pilcomayo, and the area between the Pilcomayo and the Verde River was submitted to arbitration by the President of the United States. Rutherford B. Hayes ruled on November 12, 1878 in favor of Paraguay, which in his honor renamed the former Villa Occidental as Villa Hayes.

hechos/primera-conferencia-panamericana/.texto: Between October 1889 and April 1890 the first conference of American states met in Washington, at the invitation of the United States. The Argentine delegates Roque Sáenz Peña and Manuel Quintana opposed the project of a continental customs union and, against the Monroe Doctrine’s slogan “América para los americanos,” Sáenz Peña offered that of “América para la humanidad.”

hechos/abrazo-del-estrecho/resumen.texto: On February 15, 1899 Presidents Julio A. Roca and Federico Errázuriz Echaurren met in the Strait of Magellan, opposite Punta Arenas, amid tension over boundaries and the arms race. The meeting eased the tension and opened the way to the arbitrations that followed.

hechos/litigio-de-la-puna-de-atacama/tit.texto: Arbitration of the Puna de Atacama

hechos/litigio-de-la-puna-de-atacama/res.texto: Bolivia had ceded its rights over the Puna de Atacama to Argentina in 1889, but Chile had occupied it since the War of the Pacific. In March 1899 a conference in Buenos Aires and the arbitration of the U.S. minister William Buchanan divided the territory, and most of it went to Argentina, which in 1900 created the National Territory of Los Andes there.

hechos/bloqueo-de-venezuela-1902/resumen.texto: In December 1902 Great Britain, Germany and Italy blockaded Venezuela’s ports to collect debts and claims owed to their citizens, sank Venezuelan ships and bombarded fortifications. Argentine foreign minister Luis María Drago responded with his note of December 29, and the conflict ended with the Washington protocols of 1903.

hechos/firma-de-los-pactos-de-mayo/resum.texto: On May 28, 1902 Argentina and Chile signed the May Pacts in Santiago. They submitted their differences to arbitration and limited their naval armaments, after years of arms race and threats of war over the interpretation of the 1881 treaty.

hechos/laudo-limitrofe-de-1902/resumen.texto: On November 20, 1902 King Edward VII of Great Britain issued the ruling on the disputed territories of Andean Patagonia between parallels 40 and 52, based on the report of a commission led by Thomas Holdich. It divided the disputed lands between the two countries, following neither the line of the highest peaks that Argentina asked for nor the watershed that Chile asked for. In the 16 de Octubre valley the Welsh settlers chose to remain in Argentina.

hechos/inauguracion-del-cristo-redentor/.texto: Inauguration of the Christ the Redeemer of the Andes

On March 13, 1904 the statue of Christ the Redeemer, by the sculptor Mateo Alonso, was inaugurated at the Paso de la Cumbre (La Cumbre or Bermejo), on the border between Mendoza and Chile, to celebrate peace between Argentina and Chile after the May Pacts.

hechos/generacion-del-80/resumen.texto: A group of politicians, writers and scientists who governed and wrote during the conservative order: Roca, Pellegrini, Wilde, Cané, Lucio V. López, Cambaceres, Mansilla, Groussac and Joaquín V. González, among others. They shared economic liberalism, secularism, faith in progress and positive science, and admiration for Europe, and they wrote chronicles, memoirs and novels about the transformation of Buenos Aires. For liberal historiography they were the builders of the modern state; for nationalism and revisionism, an oligarchy that handed the country over to foreign capital and excluded the majority.

hechos/positivismo-argentino/resumen.texto: From the Escuela Normal de Paraná and the Faculty of Medicine, the positivist philosophy of Comte and Spencer and Darwinian evolutionism shaped teaching, medicine, criminology and social essays between 1870 and 1915. Ramos Mejía, Bunge and Ingenieros explained Argentine history and society with biological, psychiatric and racial categories, which later criticism judged deterministic and racist.

hechos/krausismo-argentino/resumen.texto: The philosophy of the German Karl Christian Friedrich Krause, spread in the Hispanic world by Spanish Krausists and by the natural law manuals of Heinrich Ahrens, influenced the teaching of law, the pedagogy of some normal school graduates and Hipólito Yrigoyen, who knew it as a professor. Its morality of duty and its idea of an organic and harmonious society are, according to the philosopher Arturo Andrés Roig and other scholars, at the core of the discourse of early Radicalism.

hechos/fundacion-de-la-asistencia-public.texto: Creation of the Asistencia Pública of Buenos Aires

In 1883 the Buenos Aires municipality organized the Asistencia Pública, with José María Ramos Mejía as director, to coordinate free medical care, first aid, vaccination and municipal hospitals. It was one of the country’s first public health institutions.

hechos/fundacion-del-hospital-de-clinica.texto: Founding of the Hospital de Clínicas

The building of the Hospital de Clínicas, designed by engineer Mauricio Schwartz and completed in 1879, served as a barracks and as a hospital for the wounded during the June 1880 revolution. Afterward the province of Buenos Aires, defeated in the revolution, handed it over to the Faculty of Medicine, a decision the national government ratified on August 31, 1880. From then on it was the university hospital where Buenos Aires’s doctors were trained.

hechos/inauguracion-de-la-casa-de-aislam.texto: Opening of the Casa de Aislamiento (Muñiz Hospital)

On December 23, 1882 the Casa de Aislamiento was opened in Buenos Aires, on the former Quinta Leslie. It was a hospital to separate patients with contagious diseases from the rest of the population after the cholera and yellow fever epidemics. In 1904 it took the name Hospital Francisco Javier Muñiz, and until 1930 it treated mostly tuberculosis patients.

hechos/fundacion-del-museo-de-la-plata/t.texto: Founding of the Museo de La Plata

hechos/fundacion-del-museo-de-la-plata/r.texto: In 1884 the government of the province of Buenos Aires created the Museo de La Plata on the basis of the collections of Francisco P. Moreno, who directed it until 1906. Its building was inaugurated in 1888. It brought together collections of paleontology, anthropology and natural sciences, among them remains of Indigenous people who had died or been captured in the military campaigns, which since the 1990s have been returned to their communities.

hechos/graduacion-de-cecilia-grierson/ti.texto: Graduation of Cecilia Grierson, first woman physician

hechos/graduacion-de-cecilia-grierson/re.texto: In 1889 Cecilia Grierson qualified as a physician at the Faculty of Medicine of the University of Buenos Aires, the first woman to do so in the country. As a woman, she met obstacles to a teaching career at the faculty, and she devoted her work mainly to nursing, obstetrics, kinesiology and education.

hechos/fundacion-de-la-universidad-de-sa.texto: Founding of the Universidad de Santa Fe

At the initiative of governor José Gálvez, the Santa Fe legislature created the Universidad Provincial de Santa Fe in 1889, focused on law studies. In 1919 the Universidad Nacional del Litoral was created on it and other institutions of the region.

hechos/fundacion-de-la-universidad-de-la.texto: Founding of the Universidad de La Plata

The provincial university of La Plata, created by law of the province of Buenos Aires in 1890, began operating in 1897 with Dardo Rocha as rector. In 1905, through an agreement promoted by minister Joaquín V. González, the nation took it over as the Universidad Nacional de La Plata, with the museum, the observatory and agricultural schools. González presided over it until 1918.

hechos/fundacion-de-la-universidad-de-tu.texto: Founding of the Universidad de Tucumán

Created by a provincial law of 1912 at the initiative of Juan B. Terán, the Universidad de Tucumán was inaugurated on May 25, 1914, with an orientation toward technical studies and the needs of the region, such as the sugar industry. It was nationalized in 1921.

hechos/inauguracion-del-teatro-colon/tit.texto: Opening of the new Teatro Colón

hechos/inauguracion-del-teatro-colon/res.texto: On May 25, 1908 the new Teatro Colón in Buenos Aires was inaugurated with Verdi’s opera Aida, after almost twenty years of construction. It replaced the first Teatro Colón (1857-1888), facing the Plaza de Mayo, and became the center of the musical and social life of the Buenos Aires elite.

hechos/inauguracion-del-hotel-de-inmigra.texto: Opening of the Hotel de Inmigrantes

In 1911 the new Hotel de Inmigrantes was inaugurated next to the Buenos Aires port. It had been under construction since 1906 and replaced the temporary building called the Rotonda (1888-1911). There, newly arrived immigrants could stay free of charge for a few days, receive medical care and get help from an employment office to find work in the country.

lugares/colegio-nacional-de-buenos-aires.texto: Secondary school created by Mitre in 1863 on the basis of the former Colegio de Ciencias Morales, in the block of the Luces. It was the model for the national colleges of the country and trained a large part of Argentina’s leadership. Miguel Cané portrayed it in Juvenilia.

lugares/escuela-normal-de-parana/resumen.texto: First national normal school, created in Paraná in 1870 during Sarmiento’s presidency and opened in 1871 to train teachers, with directors and professors brought in part from the United States. Its graduates, the normal school teachers, spread common education throughout the country. Today it bears the name of José María Torres, one of its directors.

lugares/observatorio-de-cordoba/resumen.texto: National observatory founded in 1871 at Sarmiento’s initiative and directed in its early years by Benjamin Apthorp Gould, who catalogued the stars of the southern sky from there. It is one of the oldest scientific institutions in the country and today depends on the Universidad Nacional de Córdoba.

lugares/cementerio-de-la-chacarita/resum.texto: Cemetery opened in 1871 on the lands of the Chacarita de los Colegiales, on the outskirts of Buenos Aires, to bury the victims of the yellow fever epidemic. It is the largest cemetery in the city.

lugares/hospital-de-clinicas/resumen.texto: University hospital of the Faculty of Medicine of Buenos Aires. Its building, begun in 1877, passed to the Faculty of Medicine in 1880. Generations of Argentine doctors trained there, and in 1899 one of the first surgical operations in history was filmed there. Today it depends on the University of Buenos Aires.

lugares/hospital-muniz/resumen.texto: Infectious disease hospital in Buenos Aires, opened on December 23, 1882 as the Casa de Aislamiento, after the great cholera and yellow fever epidemics. It is named after the physician Francisco Javier Muñiz, who died in the 1871 epidemic.

lugares/universidad-nacional-del-litoral.texto: University based in Santa Fe, born from the Universidad Provincial de Santa Fe created in 1889 and nationalized in 1919 as the Universidad Nacional del Litoral. It was the first university founded after the University Reform.

lugares/universidad-nacional-de-la-plata.texto: University created by the province of Buenos Aires, which began operating in 1897 and was nationalized in 1905 on the initiative of Joaquín V. González. It incorporated the Museo de La Plata and the observatory, and from the start it focused on science and research.

lugares/universidad-nacional-de-tucuman/.texto: University created by the province of Tucumán on the initiative of Juan B. Terán, inaugurated on May 25, 1914 and nationalized in 1921. It was the first university in northwestern Argentina.

lugares/teatro-colon/resumen.texto: Opera house in Buenos Aires inaugurated in 1908, successor to the first Teatro Colón, which operated facing the Plaza de Mayo between 1857 and 1888. It is considered one of the great opera houses in the world. In June 1910 a bomb exploded in its orchestra seating, which led to the enactment of the Ley de Defensa Social.

lugares/hotel-de-inmigrantes/resumen.texto: Building erected next to the Buenos Aires port between 1906 and 1911 to receive, house, assist and direct toward work the newly arrived immigrants, who could stay there for a few days at no charge. Today it houses the Museo Nacional de la Inmigración.

lugares/cristo-redentor-de-los-andes/res.texto: Bronze statue by the sculptor Mateo Alonso, inaugurated on March 13, 1904 at the Paso de la Cumbre, on the border between Argentina and Chile, at about 3,800 meters above sea level, to celebrate the peace of the May Pacts.

lugares/fortaleza-de-humaita/resumen.texto: Paraguayan fortress built from the 1850s on a bend of the Paraguay River, near its mouth on the Paraná. Its batteries blocked the passage of ships toward Asunción. It withstood the allied siege between 1866 and 1868, and its fortifications were demolished after its fall. The ruins of its church remain.

lugares/cerro-cora/resumen.texto: Site in northeastern Paraguay, on the banks of the Aquidabán stream, where Francisco Solano López died on March 1, 1870, in the last battle of the War of the Triple Alliance. Today it is a national park.
